title: MRC/BHF Heart Protection Study of cholesterol lowering with simvastatin in 20,536 high-risk individuals: a randomised placebo-controlled trial
population: UK adults aged 40 to 80 years with coronary disease, other occlusive arterial disease or diabetes
funder: The funding statement of the 2002 report could not be read: the publisher page shows only the abstract. The 2011 report of extended follow-up of the same trial (Lancet 2011;378:2013-20) lists funding from the UK Medical Research Council, British Heart Foundation, Merck & Co and Roche Vitamins, and states that the trial was designed, conducted, analysed, and interpreted by the investigators, independently of all funding sources.
authorConflicts: The 2011 report states that the Clinical Trial Service Unit does not accept honoraria or other payments from the pharmaceutical industry, except reimbursement of the costs of scientific meetings.
result: Results read from the abstract. Simvastatin 40 mg daily (average compliance 85%) against matching placebo (average non-study statin use 17%), giving an average LDL cholesterol difference of 1.0 mmol/L. All-cause mortality 1328 (12.9%) of 10,269 allocated simvastatin against 1507 (14.7%) of 10,267 allocated placebo (p = 0.0003); coronary deaths 587 (5.7%) against 707 (6.9%). First major vascular event 2033 (19.8%) against 2585 (25.2%), a 24% reduction (95% CI 19 to 28). Annual excess risk of myopathy about 0.01%. Authors' estimate: 5 years of simvastatin would prevent about 70 to 100 people per 1000 from suffering at least one major vascular event.
